name: Sambharam
subtitle: spiced buttermilk cooler with crushed ginger, chilli and curry leaf

ingredients.note: sour yogurt makes the drink harsh
Kerala small onions, crushed not chopped
seeds removed if you want it mild
only if the yogurt is very mild
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Chill the water and the yogurt for at least an hour. Sambharam is only good cold.
Use yogurt set that morning if you can; anything older turns the drink sharp.
Crush the aromatics in a stone mortar if you have one, not a blender, for a cleaner flavour.

steps.text: Crush the shallot, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves together with the salt into a rough, wet paste.
steps.tip: The salt gives the pestle something to grip, so the aromatics bruise instead of sliding around.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt in a wide bowl for about 1 minute until it is completely smooth and pourable, with no lumps clinging to the whisk.
steps.tip: Whisk the yogurt alone first. Adding water too early leaves permanent lumps.

steps.text: Pour in the chilled water in three additions, whisking between each, until you have a thin, milky liquid.
Stir the crushed paste through the buttermilk along with the chopped coriander leaves.
Add the pinch of asafoetida if using and stir once.
Leave to stand 10 minutes at room temperature so the ginger and chilli bleed into the liquid.
steps.tip: Any longer and the shallot starts to dominate. Strain it at the 10-minute mark if you are not serving right away.

steps.text: Taste and correct the salt, adding the lemon juice only if the drink tastes flat.
Strain through a coarse sieve into a jug and serve over ice, or pour unstrained for a rougher, more rustic glass.

storage: Best within 4 hours. Keeps 1 day covered in the fridge, but strain out the aromatics first or it turns bitter. Do not freeze.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
